title: Port Blair fisheries & aquaculture: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**This is a capture-and-distribution trade before it is a farming trade.** Boats land fish at Port Blair, and cash comes from moving that catch into local markets, the tourism trade and government-linked channels; the Administration wants fish production from the Territorial Waters raised from 37% to 75% over five years [2]. **The value sits in the landing-to-market link, not in the hull.** So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower owns cold storage, ice or a market stall; if the plan is only a bigger boat, ask who buys the extra catch and at what landed price. **Aquaculture here is still subsidy-led.** Open-sea cage culture bids were invited with subsidy support, and government land is notified at a lease of Rs 1 per square metre per month, yet results are described as not fruitful [3]. Treat cage culture as a grant-dependent project, not a trading business, until the borrower shows a buyer.

## What has changed now
**Policy attention is high but delivery is unproven.** The Lt Governor has directed a revival plan for M/s Andaman Fisheries Limited, a subsidiary of ANIIDCO, modern fish markets with NFDB assistance, and joint ventures on tuna canning and marketing [2]. **None of this is contracted revenue yet.** The same review asked for subsidy schemes and intermediary crafts in phases [2], so when a proposal cites a scheme, ask for the sanction letter and the disbursement date; if the borrower has only a tender reference, treat it as pipeline. **The tender flow is real but thin on detail.** The Directorate of Fisheries Port Blair listing shows 406 live notices on one page and 516 on another [1]; that is a count of notices, not of awards, so do not read it as order flow. **Local sources say little about Port Blair's own fish volumes, prices or cold-chain capacity.** Collect from customer.

## Where the growth is
**Pursue the small operator who already lands and sells.** Target boat owners with a verified landing record, ice and cold-storage operators, and traders supplying the tourism and retail trade; the modern fish market plan [2] supports exactly this layer. **Pursue subsidy-backed cage and lease holders only with a buyer tied in.** The Rs 1 per square metre per month lease [3] keeps land cost trivial, so the risk is entirely in the stock and the sale. **Avoid the canning and tuna JV story for now.** It is a direction, not a project [2], and the peer set shows how much capital and cycle risk sits downstream: Sharat Industries grew revenue 37.89% YoY to Rs 524.72 crore for FY26 [5], while Avanti Feeds faces sticky fishmeal costs and shrimp export demand questions [7]. **Avoid disease-exposed intensive shrimp farming.** Rating commentary notes that clustering can wipe out almost 90% of a pond's shrimp population [9].

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the catch cycle, not the boat's life.** Keep tenors short, take the landing or market-sale proceeds as the repayment source, and secure against the vessel and licence. **Take every month:** landing slips or auction receipts, ice and fuel bills, the subsidy sanction status, and the lease or licence copy. **Price for the missing data.** Because the pack gives no local margin or price series, collect from customer before sanctioning any exposure above the small-ticket limit. **Peer benchmarks are for structure, not for Port Blair pricing.** Mukka Proteins saw Q1FY27 revenue up about 187% with realisations up 93% [6]; that is a fishmeal cycle, not a local catch price, so do not use it to size a Port Blair loan.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the subsidy and the buyer together.** If the scheme disbursement slips or the buyer renegotiates the landed price, cut the limit and move to monthly review. **Watch stock mortality and ice supply.** A disease event in a clustered pond [9] or a cold-chain break means stop fresh disbursement and inspect the stock. **Watch the policy promises.** If the ANIIDCO revival and fish market plans stay on paper through the next review [2], treat scheme-linked cash flows as unavailable.
watch: Volumes fall below the borrower's stated run-rate for two months -> cut limit and re-price
Sanction lapses or disbursement date slips -> stop fresh disbursement on that project
Pond or cage stock health and ice supply (fortnightly)
Mortality report or cold-chain break -> inspect stock and freeze new limits
Receivables stretch beyond the agreed cycle -> move to cash-on-delivery terms
Lease or licence lapses -> suspend the facility until renewed
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
